To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new synthetic empirical chorus model based on the combined statistics of two spacecraft missions, Van Allen Probes (2012-16) and Cluster (2001-11), and that it provides a reliable description of the chorus wave amplitude, frequency, and obliquity over the whole outer radiation belt, in particular, in the frequency range 0.1 to 12 kHz, geomagnetic latitude range 10 degrees to 45 degrees and geomagnetic activity range from quiet to moderate.
a comprehensive chorus model has been developed based on the statistical analysis of data from the Van Allan Probes and Cluster missions.

we have synthesized the chorus wave model from combined statistics from Van Allen Probes (2012- 2016) and Cluster (2001-2010) spacecraft to provide a comprehensive description of chorus wave power, obliquity and frequency in the outer radiationbelt in the form of an analytical model of chorus wave parameters as functions of latitude, Kp, and MLT.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the statistical modeling of the chorus emissions in the magnetosphere, which are among the most significant natural electromagnetic emissions as regards their effects on electron dynamics in the outer Van Allen radiation belt.
the statistical properties of chorus waves, and in particular their dependence on the geomagnetic activity level, as measured by the Kp index.
the statistical modeling of chorus wave amplitudes and obliquity in the outer radiationbelt, using data from the VanAllenProbesand Clustermissions.

this is the first time a chorus wave model based on combined statistics from two different satellite missions is presented.

the present work is the first to synthesize the data from different satellite missions to produce a reliable statistical model of chorus waves in the magnetosphere, with a good coverage in geomagnetic latitude and L-shell.
we have developed a new synthetic chorus model based on the statistics of two spacecraft missions, Van Allen Probes (Radiation Belt Storm Probes) and Cluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a new comprehensive chorus model for the outer radiation belt that is based on 4 years of VLF measurements from the Van Allen probes, complemented with 10 years from the Cluster spacecraft.
the Van Allen Proves and Cluster data are combined to provide a new empirical model of chorus waves in the magnetosphere.
the Van Allen Proves and the Cluster spacecraft have a complementary coverage for chorus waves in the outer radiation belts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive chorus model can be built by combining statistics from different missions and that this is a promising approach for future studies.

, in order to provide accurate modeling of electron dynamics in the outer radiationbelt, one needs to consider the full range of geomagnetic latitudes, from the plasmaspheric to auroral regions, and a wide range of geomagnetic activity levels.
a comprehensive model of chorus waves is crucially important to accurately model global acceleration and loss processes in the outer radiationbelt over the long run.
